vectors.description: Object keys are sorted by code point at every level; whitespace is removed.
Non-ASCII string content is written as raw UTF-8, not escaped.
Quote, backslash and C0 controls are escaped as in RFC 8785; DEL and / are not.
Integers up to +/-(2^53-1) are allowed and written in plain decimal.
Array order is kept; empty objects and arrays stay.
Floats are not allowed (use integers such as *_ppm or *_ms).
1.0 is a float in the JSON text and is refused, although its value is integral.
Exponent notation is a float.
Integers beyond 2^53-1 are refused.
Object keys must be ASCII.
Duplicate keys are refused (parsers disagree on them).
Strings must be valid Unicode; a lone surrogate escape is refused.
NaN and Infinity are not JSON.
Only the required fields: aqt, id, type, time, actor, action.
Every envelope field, including writer-owned observed and a meaning.
x-<org>. types are valid envelopes (registration is checked at conformance L1).
A record signed by the RFC 8032 TEST 1 key; the signature covers the record without sig.
Two independent signatures; only TEST 1 is pinned, so TEST 2 reports unknown (null).
The envelope is still valid, but the signature no longer verifies (false).
Unknown top-level fields are invalid; extensions go into data.
aqt must be "0.1".
id is rec_ plus 28 lower-case hex digits.
type is <tool>.<kind> in lower case.
time is UTC with a Z suffix; offsets go into tz as a zone name.
actor is required.
actor.kind is human, agent or service.
meaning comes from the fixed vocabulary.
reason, when present, is non-blank.
subject needs kind and ref.
sha256 values are sha256:<64 lower-case hex>.
chain.seq is an integer.
sig entries use alg ed25519.
links are {rel, ref}.
No floats anywhere, also inside data; the schema alone cannot see this.
Duplicate keys make a record ambiguous and invalid.
A lone surrogate in a string makes the record invalid.
Four records chained from GENESIS (64 zeros).
The same chain, each record signed by TEST 1; signatures required.
Record 1 edited: without signatures the break shows at the next record (seq 2), whose prev no longer matches.
Record 1 edited in a signed chain: its own signature fails (seq 1).
LIMIT: editing the last record of an unsigned chain is not detectable by the chain alone; signatures or a checkpoint are needed.
Record 1 deleted: record seq 2 appears where seq 1 is expected.
Records 0 and 1 swapped.
A record from another chain inserted at position 2.
The first record's prev is not GENESIS.
LIMIT: dropping the last record leaves a valid shorter chain; only a checkpoint detects it (see checkpoint/truncated).
A complete rewrite signed with another key verifies as a chain but fails against the pinned key (no valid signature from a known key at seq 0).
Signatures required, but the records carry none.
A signed checkpoint of the head (seq 3) that matches the chain.
The chain was truncated after the checkpoint: no record at seq 3 any more, so the checkpoint does not match.
A rewritten chain has another head hash at seq 3.
The checkpoint's seq was changed after signing.
A checkpoint signed by a key that is not pinned is not valid.
A detached signed statement over a record's content hash (record_content_hash excludes sig, chain, observed and time), so it still matches after the trail stored it.
The statement still verifies, but the signed record's content changed: the signature no longer applies to it (invalidated).
The meaning inside the statement was changed after signing.
Signed by a key that is not pinned: unknown (null).
